steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition to ON so the center screen wakes up.
Touch the Settings icon, then touch Maintenance.
Make sure Maintenance Reminders is turned on.
Touch Oil Change, then touch Reset to restart the reminder.
To change when it reminds you, touch Next Service Date or Interval Distance, adjust it, and touch Set.

Turn the ignition to ON so the center screen wakes up.
Press HOME, then touch the Car Info icon.
In the second menu of the car info screen, touch Maintenance, then Engine Oil.
Touch Reset to reset the oil reminder.
To change when it reminds you, choose Notification Date or Notification Distance, adjust it, and touch Set.
oil.note: Update puts the item back to its default value. Reminders only show if Maintenance is turned on under the Reminder Screen setting in General settings.

tpms.when: 2026 (U.S. models; no driver reset, the light clears itself)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Drive at 25 mph or more. That starts the system re-checking the pressures.
If all tires are properly inflated, the light goes out on its own. There is no reset button.
tpms.note: If the light blinks for about a minute and then stays on, the system has a fault that no reset will clear; have a Subaru dealer check it. If a wheel is changed without moving its sensor over, the light also blinks then stays on until a dealer services the system. The owner's manual lists this light for all models except Canadian ones.

tpms.when: 2024 (U.S. models; no driver reset, the light clears itself)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Drive the car. Once the system detects the corrected pressures, the light turns off on its own.
If it stays on, recheck each tire with a gauge; one may still be low.
tpms.note: The owner's manual gives no reset button or menu for this light; it is listed for U.S. models. If the tire pressure light flashes for about a minute when you start the car and then stays on, the warning system itself has a fault. A reset won't fix it; have it checked.
